pct.$comment: Here the `primary` ramp goes UP (lighter on hover/active), the opposite of the light theme. The reason is measurable, not aesthetic: in the dark theme `on-primary` is DARK, so darkening the background drives the label's contrast down instead of up — that once gave 3.45:1 on hover and 2.66:1 on active, below AA, with a green build. The same token is also text on a dark surface (the outline variant's label), and that needs a light step: blue.500 on `surface-100` gave 3.98:1.

hero-text.$comment: The gradient as TEXT, lifted for the dark ground. The surface stops (`hero`, `hero-via`, `hero-to`) are NOT overridden here on purpose — the brand's gradient is the same blue on both themes, and it is only the word cut out of it that has to move: 7.02, 6.56 and 7.35 against `surface`, where the unlifted stops read 3.45, 3.13 and 3.33.

pct.$comment-danger: The dark theme's `danger`, and nothing moved here: the light theme's base stepped from `600` to `700` for a pair measured on a light ground, while this end of the ramp already carried every pair it had to. What is new is the family — the resting fill, its hover and its press go UP the ramp rather than down, because a dark ground lightens what stands on it, and the text over them is the ramp's far end (`slate.1000`) rather than white.
pct.$comment-tones: The same family the light theme gained, read off the other end of the ramps. Three readings say why the direction inverts: measured on `slate.900` the bases are 10.25:1, 10.69:1 and 7.02:1, which a `700` step could not reach here. The soft face inverts with them — `800` is the resting tint and `700` its hover, with the ramp's lightest step as the label, and the two tightest pairs in the whole skin are here (`warning` 4.51:1 and `success` 4.57:1 on that hover tint), which is a note for whoever next touches these two steps. The rest of the reason stands with the light theme's: a tone is never only a colour, and on a button the second channel is the label (0076, 0053).
pct.$comment-info: Info is the brand blue, and deliberately the same value as `primary`: an informational message is not an alarm, the skin has exactly one calm accent, and a fourth hue invented for it would be a colour with no meaning behind it. The name is separate because the ROLE is — a theme that recolours its brand should not have to think about what that does to a message. The family below is its own for the same reason, and is written out rather than pointed at `primary`: a skin where the two diverge changes seven values here and nothing anywhere else.
pct.$comment-scrim: The veil, and here it has to be the ramp's endpoint rather than `slate.900`: the dark theme's page IS `slate.900`, so a veil of the same step would dim it by nothing at all. How translucent it is, and how far the page behind it is blurred, are the component's two other tokens — all three are the skin's to set.
pct.$comment-surface-inverse: The surface that answers the page rather than joining it — dark on a light theme and light on a dark one. It exists for the annotation kind of panel (the tooltip is the first): a surface a reader is meant to notice for a moment and then stop seeing, which the ordinary `surface` cannot be, being what the page is made of. The `on-` pair is not decoration here — an inverted surface is the one place where reaching for `pct.text` by reflex paints text the same colour as the box it stands in.
